title: Override the injectable LocalDayClock in backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time assertions

evidence.quote: final now = DateTime.now(); / final lastSynced = now.subtract(const Duration(seconds: 30));

why: _formatTimeAgo reads DateTimeFactory.nowLocal(), which resolves through the overridable localDayClockProvider — a FakeLocalDayClock already exists in lib/core/time/local_day_clock.dart for exactly this purpose. This file never overrides it: it seeds 'just now'/'Xm ago' assertions from real DateTime.now() at 5 call sites (lines 155, 179, 201, 227, 657), then the widget independently re-reads the clock a pump later. Today's margins (e.g. a 30s buffer under the 60s 'just now' cliff) make an actual flake unlikely, but the suite is non-deterministic by construction and the gap between test-now and widget-build-now is unbounded on a loaded/slow CI runner.
recommendation: In _buildHarness, call useLocalDayClock(FakeLocalDayClock(fixedInstant)) (or override localDayClockProvider) and derive lastSynced from that same fixed instant, removing the wall-clock dependency entirely.
acceptance_criteria: backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time tests construct lastSyncedAt from a fixed instant and override localDayClockProvider/useLocalDayClock to that same instant.
The suite still passes with no bare DateTime.now() feeding a time-relative text assertion.

corrections: Line 657's test ('cloud-born already synced on mount does NOT kick another pull') asserts only verifyNever(pullOnLaunch), not relative-time text, so 'sites:5' overcounts by one for the specific 'just now'/'Xm ago' assertion claim. Also, DateTimeFactory.nowLocal() is gated by the global currentLocalDayClock (set via useLocalDayClock()), not by the Riverpod localDayClockProvider — overriding the latter alone would not fix this widget's read.

'sites: 5' overcounts by one — line 657's DateTime.now() feeds a test that only asserts pullOnLaunch is NOT called again (verified lines 654-678); it makes no relative-time text assertion, so it isn't one of the wall-clock-sensitive sites the 'why' claims. True count is 4 (155, 179, 201, 227); the underlying defect and recommendation stand unaffected.
